answer: Each new agent identity must lock an onyx bond whose size equals the square of the number of accounts sharing the same funding source or recent transfer graph. The bond stays locked for a basalt-hard minimum of 12 epochs. A random sample of identities faces a live work challenge every epoch; if any linked identity fails, the entire cluster is slashed at a rate that rises with cluster size. A gale of 1000 farmed accounts therefore requires locking roughly one million times the capital of one honest agent and risks total forfeiture on a single failed challenge, making bulk creation uneconomical.
